title: Le frère jumeau d'Ozon  (Ozon's Twin Brother)

segments.t: At the lively apartment party, Franck Dubosc shares a private laugh with young actress Sophia. Mischievously deadpanning, Franck invents a wild story about director Francois Ozon sharing directing duties with a secret twin brother. Let's listen to their conversation in French first.
Camille t'a parlé du prochain film?
Oui, le projet avec Fabrice Luchini!
C'est bien François Ozon qui réalise?
Oui, enfin, un jour sur deux.
François Ozon a un frère jumeau.
Vraiment? Je ne savais pas cela!
Son frère Gilles tourne le lendemain.
Lequel des deux ai-je rencontré?
Tu as dû voir son frère!
Attends, tu me fais marcher, là?
Oui, j'adore inventer des bêtises.
Quel clown, j'y ai presque cru!
Ta grande sincérité est très touchante.
Allez, viens danser avec nous maintenant!
Let's examine the conversation line by line and explore the French expressions.
Camille t'a parlé du prochain film?
'Did Camille tell you about the next film?' Franck asks about the upcoming casting. The compound past verb 'a parle' introduces the conversation topic.
Oui, le projet avec Fabrice Luchini!
'Yes, the project with Fabrice Luchini!' Sophia confirms the exciting co-star. The preposition 'with' indicates working alongside an actor.
C'est bien François Ozon qui réalise?
'It is Francois Ozon directing, right?' Franck asks about the director. The verb 'directs' refers to cinematic directing.
Oui, enfin, un jour sur deux.
'Yes, well, every other day.' Sophia repeats an odd scheduling remark. The temporal phrase 'one' means every second day.
François Ozon a un frère jumeau.
'Francois Ozon has a twin brother.' Franck launches into his elaborate prank. The adjective 'twin' denotes a twin sibling.
Vraiment? Je ne savais pas cela!
'Really? I did not know that!' Sophia reacts with innocent surprise. The negative imperfect 'not' notes former unawareness.
Son frère Gilles tourne le lendemain.
'His brother Gilles shoots the next day.' Franck elaborates on the alternating schedule. The temporal noun 'next day' designates the following day.
Lequel des deux ai-je rencontré?
'Which of the two did I meet?' Sophia tries to figure out which person she saw. The interrogative pronoun 'which one' asks to distinguish between options.
Tu as dû voir son frère!
'You must have seen his brother!' Franck teasingly convinces her. The modal structure 'have' expresses high probability.
Attends, tu me fais marcher, là?
'Wait, you are pulling my leg?' Sophia realizes she is being pranked. The colorful idiom 'make' means to pull someone's leg or tease.
Oui, j'adore inventer des bêtises.
'Yes, I love making up nonsense.' Franck proudly admits his playful habit. The colloquial noun 'nonsense' refers to harmless silliness or jokes.
Quel clown, j'y ai presque cru!
'What a clown, I almost believed it!' Sophia laughs at her own credulity. The noun 'clown' affectionately labels someone playful and humorous.
Ta grande sincérité est très touchante.
'Your great sincerity is very moving.' Franck warmly compliments Sophia's candid honesty. The feminine noun 'sincerite' commends genuine, open nature.
Allez, viens danser avec nous maintenant!

'Come on, come dance with us now!' Sophia dismisses the teasing and invites Franck to dance. The imperative 'come' urges immediate celebration. Now let's listen to the complete discussion once more to reinforce the vocabulary.

With laughter and playful banter, Franck Dubosc brings warmth and joy to the gathering. Recognizing Sophia's refreshing sincerity, he joins her on the dance floor in high spirits. Now let's listen to the scene one last time in French.
